decisions.reason: This cutting and creasing finisher sits close to the core offer and has its own product page, so management sees no reason to withdraw it so soon after launch, though its low visibility makes it easier to drop than the flagships.

The UV spot varnishing system was launched as a publicly staged German premiere and presented as a flagship of the firm's direction, so dropping it would write off a visible investment and expose the move into an adjacent field as a mistake.
The sheet preparation module builds on the established portfolio and supports the automated workflow the firm has announced, so little speaks for removing it.
The B2 multifinisher is featured on the home page as the firm's new flagship solution and fits its core business, so the firm is strongly committed to it.
The hybrid saddle stitcher is close to the core booklet-making business and has its own page, so it is likely to stay in the portfolio for now.
The folding add-on has received only a passing mention and little public commitment, but a documented customer installation shows it works, so keeping it as a low-cost complement is reasonable.
